Calculate the temporal range of fossil taxa

Source: R/tax_range_time.R
tax_range_time.Rd

A function to calculate the temporal range of fossil taxa from occurrence data.

Usage

tax_range_time(
  data,
  name = "genus",
  min_ma = "min_ma",
  max_ma = "max_ma",
  group = NULL,
  sort = "FAD",
  by = deprecated(),
  plot = deprecated(),
  plot_args = deprecated(),
  intervals = deprecated()
)

# S3 method for class 'palaeoverse_tax_range_time'
plot(
  x,
  ...,
  axis = axis_geo(side = 1, intervals = "periods", title = xlab),
  main = "Temporal range of taxa",
  xlab = "Time (Ma)",
  ylab = "Taxon",
  col.group = c("grey85", "grey95")
)

Arguments

data

dataframe. A dataframe of fossil occurrences containing at least three columns: names of taxa, minimum age and maximum age (see name, min_ma, and max_ma arguments). These ages should constrain the age range of the fossil occurrence and are assumed to be in millions of years before present.

name

character. The name of the column you wish to be treated as the input names, e.g. "genus" (default).

min_ma

character. The name of the column you wish to be treated as the minimum limit of the age range, e.g. "min_ma" (default).

max_ma

character. The name of the column you wish to be treated as the maximum limit of the age range, e.g. "max_ma" (default).

group

character. The name of the column you wish to be treated as the grouping variable, e.g. "family". If not supplied, all taxa are treated as a single group.

sort

character. How should the output be sorted? Either: "FAD" (first-appearance date; default), "LAD" (last-appearance data), or "name" (alphabetically by taxon names).

by

Use sort instead.

plot, plot_args

Use plot() on the output of this function instead.

intervals

Use the argument axis in plot() on the output of this function instead.

x

data.frame. An object of class "palaeoverse_tax_range_time" created by tax_range_time().

...

Extra graphical parameters (see Details). The following arguments are already set internally and must not be specified here: xlim, ylim, xaxt, yaxt.

axis

A function call drawing an axis, such as axis_geo() (default) to add the geological timescale at the bottom of the plot, or graphics::axis().

main

character. The plot title.

xlab

character. The x-axis title.

ylab

character. The y-axis title.

col.group

character. The background colours to use when x has groups. Must be of the same length as the number of unique groups.

Value

A data.frame containing the following columns: unique taxa (taxon), taxon ID (taxon_id), first appearance of taxon (max_ma), last appearance of taxon (min_ma), duration of temporal range (range_myr), and number of occurrences per taxon (n_occ) is returned.

This data.frame has an attribute palaeoverse_tax_range_time_group that is for internal use only.

plot() invisibly returns a list with the graphical parameters mar and usr used to draw the plot (see graphics::par()).

Details

The temporal range(s) of taxa are calculated by extracting all unique taxa (name column) from the input data, and checking their first and last appearance. The temporal duration of each taxon is also calculated. If the input data columns contain NAs, these must be removed prior to function call.

Note: this function provides output based solely on the user input data. The true duration of a taxon is likely confounded by uncertainty in dating occurrences, and incomplete sampling and preservation.

The following graphical parameters have default values that differ from base R:

  • bg = "black": the background (fill) colour of the points, only used for pch values 21 to 25.

  • pch = 20: the symbol used for the first and last appearance points (see graphics::points()).

  • yaxs = "i": the style of y-axis interval calculation (see graphics::par()).

The graphical parameters are reset when plot() exits. See 'Examples' to know how to add components to the plot.

Examples

# Grab internal data
data <- tetrapods
# Remove NAs
data <- subset(data, !is.na(order) & order != "NO_ORDER_SPECIFIED")
# Temporal range
ex <- tax_range_time(data = data, name = "order")
plot(ex)


# Temporal range ordered by class
# Update margins for plotting
par(mar = c(8, 5, 6, 6))
ex <- tax_range_time(data = data, name = "order", group = "class")
plot(ex)


# Customise appearance
ex <- tax_range_time(data = data, name = "order", group = "class")
plot(ex, ylab = "Orders", pch = 21, col = "black", bg = "blue", lty = 2,
     axis = axis_geo(intervals = "eras", abbr = FALSE))


# Control plotting order of groups
data$class <- factor(x = data$class,
                      levels = c("Reptilia", "Osteichthyes"))
ex <- tax_range_time(data = data, name = "order", group = "class")
plot(ex)

# Add elements to the plot
op <- par(plot(ex))
abline(v = 290, lty = 2, col = "red")

par(op)
